Request Description
Test ID: API-081 Category: SECURITY Objective: Verify that SQL syntax in a rule-conforming new password is treated as data and does not damage another account's reset path. Flow step: Step 1 - Account A injection string Preconditions / Setup: After the initialized SUT is running, the direct-SQLite fixture seeds poola-api-081-a@example.test with reset_token stored as exact TEXT 100081. Accounts A and B are registered. Each has its own valid, unexpired, unused six-digit OTP. The password Aa1!';DROP TABLE users;-- satisfies the documented minimum rules through its uppercase, lowercase, digit, allowed exclamation mark, and length. The same fixture seeds the independent second account poola-api-081-b@example.test with different exact TEXT OTP 200081. Reviewed request input: Step 1: Send POST /api/reset-password with Content-Type: application/json and body {"email":"poola-api-081-a@example.test","resetToken":"100081","newPassword":"Aa1!';DROP TABLE users;--"}. Step 2: Independently send POST /api/reset-password with Content-Type: application/json and body {"email":"poola-api-081-b@example.test","resetToken":"200081","newPassword":"OrdinaryReset1!"}. Verify Account A with the first password and Account B with the second password. Reviewed expected result: Account A's reset succeeds and the supplied password is treated only as data. Account B's reset also succeeds, demonstrating that the injected password did not damage the users data path. Specification basis: Main_Report.md section A.7 human case API-081; SEC-05 SQL-injection resistance; reviewed password rules. Assumptions / Notes: Human-authored case. The second account provides an observable integrity check; proving parameterized storage may still require implementation or database inspection. Preconditions / Setup: After the initialized SUT is running, the direct-SQLite fixture seeds poola-api-082@example.test with reset_token stored as exact TEXT 100082. Do not omit the Authorization header and do not replace the garbage token with a valid JWT. Reviewed expected result: The reset succeeds with 200 OK. The invalid JWT does not affect this public recovery endpoint.
